claim: In a vanilla RNN, the gradient from step t back to step k is a product of W_rec^T diag(sigma'(x)) terms, one per step.
If the largest eigenvalue of W_rec is below 1 (with bounded activation derivative), long-term gradient components vanish; it must exceed 1 for gradients to explode.
Gradient norm clipping is the proposed remedy for exploding gradients.
The original LSTM's memory cell connects to itself with a fixed weight of 1.0 and a one-step delay; this is the constant error carousel (CEC).
Multiplicative gate units learn to open and close access to the constant error flow.
The 1997 LSTM bridged minimal time lags of more than 1000 discrete time steps, including on noisy, incompressible input sequences.
Compared with RTRL, BPTT, recurrent cascade correlation, Elman nets and neural sequence chunking, the 1997 LSTM had many more successful runs and learned much faster.
The 1997 LSTM had no forget gate and truncated the gradient at certain architecture-specific points to keep error flow constant.
Without resets, an LSTM's cell state can grow indefinitely on continual input streams and eventually break the network.
The forget gate (2000) lets a cell learn to reset itself; LSTM with forget gates solved continual benchmark versions that all other algorithms, including the original LSTM, failed.
Across 5400 runs (about 15 CPU-years) of eight LSTM variants on speech, handwriting and music, no variant significantly improved on the standard LSTM.
The forget gate and the output activation function are the standard LSTM's most critical components.
Standard LSTM uses sigmoid gate activations and usually tanh for block input and output activations.
An architecture search over more than ten thousand RNN architectures found one that beat LSTM and GRU on some but not all tasks.
Initialising the forget-gate bias to 1 closes the gap between the LSTM and the GRU.
In ablations, the input gate is important, the output gate is unimportant, and the forget gate is extremely significant on all problems except language modelling.
A forget-gate-only LSTM outperformed the full three-gate LSTM on all five tasks tested.
Along the direct cell path, d c_t / d c_{t-1} = diag(f_t), so the long-range factor is a product of forget-gate values with no weight matrix or tanh derivative.
Worked example over 50 steps: RNN factor 0.54 gives 4.2e-14; LSTM with f=0.5 gives 8.9e-16; f=sigmoid(1)=0.73 gives 1.6e-7; f=0.99 gives 0.61; f=1 gives 1.0.
For m=128 inputs and n=256 hidden units, a vanilla RNN layer has 98,560 parameters and an LSTM layer 394,240 (4x); PyTorch reports 395,264 because it keeps two bias vectors per gate.
